task: L1 - cost-of-soundness ladder: one admitted set (the 1,728 reads cache_identity admits), one ingredient per rung, with hits, hit rate and unsafe hits measured from the replay
scope: tau-bench only: the first trial of every task in the committed corpus, four source runs, replayed through run-scope caches. The main ladder scores one admitted set (the 1,728 reads cache_identity admits) and adds one soundness ingredient per rung; the mirror ladder repeats the rungs with all 2,275 calls admitted. Unsafe hits are counted from the replay, never estimated.

identity_module.why_imported: the admitted set is its effect map, every digest on the ladder is one of its key recipes, and every eviction is its index; re-deriving any of them here is how a ladder drifts from the cache it claims to measure

main.admitted_set: reads only, the ladder's admitted set: the 1,728 calls cache_identity admits (given before rung 0, so identical at every rung)

rungs.label: blind key
rungs.note: sha256 over the tool and its canonical arguments: the published reuse recipe's identity notion. A hit is always the same question, and says nothing about who asked or whether the answer still holds.

rungs.label: blind key + tenant
rungs.note: the tenant enters the digest, so one tenant cannot be answered with another's row. key_typed also domain-separates and refuses non-reads; on a reads-only admitted set neither can move a hit, and tenant_ingredient_isolated checks that rather than assuming it.

rungs.label: + entity invalidation
rungs.note: a stored read is filed under every entity id it names; a write that lands evicts the keys filed under the ids it names, so a surviving key names no entity the write named.

rungs.label: + read-only admission (given)
rungs.ingredient_added: read-only admission -- already the baseline, adds nothing here
rungs.note: the admission gate is what defines this ladder's denominator, so it was paid before rung 0 and this rung must reproduce L2 exactly. Its price is measured on the mirror ladder (M2 -> M3), where the same corpus is admitted in full.

mirror.admitted_set: all 2,275 calls at M0-M2 (writes and control tools admitted); reads only at M3, the admission rung

rungs.label: blind key
rungs.note: every call stored and served, nothing evicted: the P1 baseline.

rungs.label: blind key + tenant
rungs.key: key_tenant_blind(tool, args, tenant) = cache_identity.key_blind([tenant, tool], args)
rungs.note: the tenant in the key, on a cache that admits writes -- so the key cannot be key_typed, which refuses to key a write at all.

rungs.label: + entity invalidation
rungs.note: freshness is handled for reads, but a write's own memo is never filed in the index (only reads are), so a repeated write is still served.

rungs.label: + read-only admission
rungs.note: the same chain measured on the 2,275 denominator: refuses the 446 writes and 101 control calls, and is therefore L2 restated. The M2 -> M3 gap is what admitting writes adds.

committed_typed_policy.why: L3 must reproduce the committed typed replay; the anchor is pinned so a drift in either artifact fails the checks instead of moving a paper number

published_reuse.why: L0 is that recipe's identity notion restricted to reads; the ladder decomposes a stricter cache, it does not re-derive 41.70%

provenance.determinism: no clock, no environment, no randomness, no git lookup; JSON-native arguments; every collection emitted in a stable order; every rung replayed twice and the documents compared before writing
provenance.arithmetic: integer counts; rates are round(numerator/denominator, 4); point deltas round(., 2); no weighted averages

definitions.admitted_set: the calls a rung stores: the 1,728 effect-class reads on the main ladder, all 2,275 calls on mirror rungs M0-M2, reads again at M3. Admission is decided by cache_identity.effect_class before any key is computed.
definitions.rung: one point on a ladder. Adjacent rungs differ by exactly one ingredient -- the tenant in the key, then entity invalidation, then read-only admission -- so the delta between them is attributable.
definitions.hit: an admitted call whose key is already in the rung's run-scope cache; the memo is returned and the tool does not run
definitions.hit_rate: hits / admitted_calls of the same rung, rounded to 4 decimals. The main ladder's denominator is 1,728 for every rung, which is what makes its rungs comparable; hit_rate_of_all_calls divides by 2,275 and is reported so both ladders can be read on one base.
definitions.writes_served: an unsafe hit where the call is a write: the mutation is answered from a memo and never runs, while the agent's belief that it ran is unchanged
definitions.stale_read: an unsafe hit where the call is a read and some write that executed names an entity id the read names, at a position strictly between the memo's store position and the hit; the memo predates the write
definitions.cross_tenant: an unsafe hit where the call is a read, the memo was stored under a different known tenant, and the hit is not already stale. An unknown tenant on either side is never counted, so this class is a lower bound
definitions.unsafe_hit: the union of writes_served, stale_reads and cross_tenant, each hit assigned to exactly one class by the precedence writes_served > stale_reads > cross_tenant, so the breakdown sums to the total. unsafe_by_class_overlapping keeps the pre-precedence counts where a hit falls in more than one class.
definitions.ingredient: one of the three soundness ingredients the committed policies bundle: the tenant in the key (identity), entity invalidation (freshness), and read-only admission (effect). The ladder orders them tenant -> invalidation -> admission.
definitions.marginal_cost: hit_rate_before - hit_rate_after, in percentage points, and unsafe_before - unsafe_after, in hits, for one adjacent pair. Positive points lost and positive unsafe removed are the cost and the benefit of that one ingredient.
definitions.point: one percentage point of hit rate on the rung's denominator. Every point quoted is measured on 1,728 main-ladder calls or 2,275 mirror calls; no rate is averaged across rungs or runs.
definitions.control_hits: hits on control tools (think, transfer_to_human_agents). They are admitted and memoised on mirror rungs M0-M2, refused on M3 and by every main rung, and are not one of the three unsafe classes
definitions.not_counted: reads naming no entity id cannot be joined to a write; unknown tenants cannot be compared; a failed write is indistinguishable from a landed one in this corpus and is treated as landed. Each gap can only understate unsoundness.

entity invalidation: costs 8.85 points of hit rate on 1,728 calls (35.82% -> 26.97%) and removes 168 unsafe hits (stale_reads 168).

read_hits_from_unexecuted_writes.why: a write served from cache never ran, so it evicted nothing: some reads that M3 would have re-read after the mutation are still answered from the memo. These extra read hits are a second-order effect of the writes_served defect, not a separate unsoundness class, and they are why the hits admitting writes buys exceed the write hits themselves

what_admitting_writes_adds.statement: admitting writes and control tools buys 71 extra hits (3.12 points on 2,275 calls) and adds 60 unsafe hits that no key or eviction ingredient removes

admitted_set.why: cache_identity admits only effect-class read tools; the 446 writes and 101 control calls are refused before the lookup, which is exactly the typed policy's admission decision

write_repeats_independent.why: a write's own memo is never filed in the eviction index (only reads are), so no eviction can remove it: writes_served must be unchanged from M1 to M2 and, on the blind rung, must equal the corpus's repeated-write count. M0 can exceed M1 only by pairing two identical writes the tenant separates -- one of them is a call whose record names no user

typed_key_neutrality.why: key_typed(tool, args, None) is a bijective relabelling of key_blind's digest classes, so switching recipe without adding the tenant cannot move a hit; any L0 -> L1 difference is therefore the tenant

mirror_key_agreement.why: the mirror's write-capable tenant key, replayed over reads only, must hit exactly as key_typed does; that is what isolates M2 -> M3 as an admission change rather than a key change

typed_policy_anchor.why: L3 is the typed policy, so the ladder's top rung must reproduce the committed P4 replay; a mismatch means the ladder stopped measuring the cache the paper describes

admitted_set_is_1728.detail: main rungs admit [1728] of 2275 calls; reads=1728

one_admitted_set.detail: every main rung scores the same calls on the same streams

no_non_reads_admitted_on_main.detail: a write or control hit on the main ladder would mean the admitted set leaked

mirror_not_cleared_before_admission.detail: M2=60 unsafe with the tenant and invalidation both in place; only read-only admission clears it

rung3_is_the_baseline_not_a_change.detail: L3 restates L2 by construction: admission was given before rung 0

write_repeats_match.detail: repeated write keys 61 = M0 61; M1 60 == M2 60, so eviction removes no write's own memo

breakdown_sums.detail: unsafe_hits == sum of its three classes

rates_are_exact_ratios.detail: every rate is round(numerator/denominator, 4); unsafe never exceeds hits

deterministic_replay.detail: every rung replayed twice and the two documents compared before writing
